documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs (Instructional Faculty Academic Policy Manual; Academic Integrity Policy)
documents.title: Kean University Instructional Faculty Academic Policy Manual and Resource Guide, Fall 2025: Expectations of Generative AI
documents.date_or_term: Fall 2025 (AI text from the Academic Integrity Policy, Fall 2024 revision)
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single university stance: "faculty members specify in their course syllabi how AI and GenAI may be used" and "These guidelines may vary from course to course." Only baseline rules (no AI as original work, citation where permitted) apply to all, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: Kean's faculty manual reproduces the university's AI statement from its Academic Integrity Policy (Fall 2024). Each instructor sets AI rules in the syllabus, while universal rules apply everywhere: AI output is not original student work, must be cited where AI is allowed, and must be reviewed by students, with misuse handled as an integrity violation. The manual also advises faculty on how much AI to permit and how to handle suspected misuse.

units.why: This is the definitional passage: "Generative AI (GenAI) includes programs such as ChatGPT, GPT 4, DALL-E, Quillbot, Vertex" fixes which tools the policy covers, so it is general-phase, informs, and P61 (define AI and scope).
units.anchor: Generative AI (GenAI) includes programs such as ChatGPT, GPT 4, DALL-E, Quillbot, Vertex

units.why: The sentence states that "faculty members specify in their course syllabi how AI and GenAI may be used"; this is a university requirement that instructors state AI expectations in the syllabus, so actor instructor, phase course-start, must, P09 (not P04, which is about who decides).
units.anchor: faculty members specify in their course syllabi how AI and GenAI may be used
units.frag_start: At Kean University, faculty members specify
units.frag_end: may be used in their classes.

units.why: "These guidelines may vary from course to course" tells readers that the rule is set course by course rather than by one university rule, so it is P04 (let each instructor set the rule); informs because it describes the arrangement.
units.anchor: These guidelines may vary from course to course.

units.why: "Students are required to adhere to the specific requirements outlined in each syllabus" binds students to the instructor-set rule, so actor student, must, P04 (the instructor-set course rule governs); P11 is not chosen because the sentence does not say permissions do not carry over.
units.anchor: Students are required to adhere to the specific requirements outlined in each syllabus.

units.why: The overarching guideline "Content created by Generative AI cannot be presented as original student work" bars passing off AI output as one's own, so student, must-not, P19, prohibit.
units.anchor: Content created by Generative AI cannot be presented as original student work.

units.why: "any content generated by AI must be cited and attributed" (in courses where AI is permitted) is a disclosure/citation duty on students, so student, must, P24; unit_stance permit because it conditions permitted use.
units.anchor: any content generated by AI must be cited and attributed

units.why: "just like ideas, text, speech, or imagery from human authors" compares AI-generated content to human sources under existing citation norms, so P45 (treat AI like a human source), informs.
units.anchor: cited and attributed just like ideas, text, speech, or imagery from human authors

units.why: "This includes the use of quotation marks, citations, and other forms of attribution to clearly distinguish" sets how attribution must look, requiring students to mark AI-generated material; student, must, P24 (it states no tool/prompt detail so not P25).
units.anchor: This includes the use of quotation marks, citations, and other forms of

units.why: "Students are accountable for any content they create or publish" puts responsibility on the student for submitted content, so student, must, P29 (students own what they submit).
units.anchor: Students are accountable for any content they create or publish.

units.why: "AI-generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, fabricated (referred to as hallucinations)" is a factual warning about AI output reliability, so informs, P31.
units.anchor: can be inaccurate, misleading, fabricated

units.why: The passage warns AI content may "include copyrighted material", a licensing/copyright concern stated as fact, so informs and P52.
units.anchor: or include copyrighted material.

units.why: "students must meticulously review all AI-generated content" (if faculty policy permits AI) obliges students to verify output, so student, must, P31, permit because it conditions allowed use.
units.anchor: students must meticulously review all AI-generated content

units.why: "acknowledging their responsibility for the accuracy of any work they submit" makes students answerable for accuracy of submitted work, so student, must, P29 (ownership) rather than P31 (verification, coded in the previous unit).
units.anchor: acknowledging their responsibility for the accuracy of any work they submit

units.why: "Faculty may use various tools and methods to ensure appropriate use of AI, including: ... AI detection tools integrated into Canvas" authorizes detector and comparison checks, so instructor, may, P40 (not P39, which says do not rely on detectors).
units.anchor: AI detection tools integrated into Canvas
units.policy: Faculty may use comparisons with in-class or other written work and AI detection tools integrated into Canvas to ensure appropriate use of AI.

units.why: "demonstrated mastery of learning via the ability to orally present/discuss content" names oral explanation as evidence of appropriate AI use; instructor, may, P34 (checking understanding by oral discussion).
units.anchor: demonstrated mastery of learning via the ability to orally present/discuss content

units.why: "Use contrary to the course policy and/or without proper acknowledgement is subject to the same rules and consequences outlined for integrity violations" classifies misuse as an academic integrity violation, so P36, informs.
units.anchor: is subject to the same rules and consequences outlined for integrity violations

units.why: "Consequences of inappropriate use may include failing the assignment, failing the course, and/or further disciplinary actions" lists concrete penalties, so P37, informs (may include).
units.anchor: failing the assignment, failing the course, and/or further disciplinary actions

units.why: "Students are encouraged to use student academic support services available at Kean to develop their skills and avoid reliance on Generative AI tools" discourages reliance without banning AI, so P03, should, student; unit_stance restrict as the closest enum for a mild limit.
units.anchor: to develop their skills and avoid reliance on Generative AI tools

units.why: "supporting students as they learn to appropriately navigate key life tools, such as Artificial Intelligence" frames learning to use AI as part of student success, a professional/life-skill rationale, so P44, informs.
units.anchor: supporting students as they learn to appropriately navigate key life tools, such as Artificial Intelligence

units.why: "Students uncertain about AI use expectations in a course should seek clarification from their instructors" tells students to ask when unsure, so student, should, P10.
units.anchor: should seek clarification from their instructors

units.why: "Failure to seek clarification is not an acceptable excuse to challenge an academic integrity violation" removes uncertainty as a defense, reinforcing the ask-first rule (P10) rather than describing sanctions (P36); modality informs.
units.anchor: Failure to seek clarification is not an acceptable excuse

units.why: "faculty are encouraged to clearly define their course-specific expectations for AI use in their syllabi and on individual assignments" recommends instructors state expectations, so instructor, should, P09.
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to clearly define their course-specific expectations for AI use

units.why: "Faculty should familiarize themselves with how artificial intelligence (AI) is used in their respective fields" advises instructors to learn about AI before setting course expectations, so instructor, should, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty should familiarize themselves with how artificial intelligence (AI) is used

units.why: "the amount of generative AI use you allow in your class depends on your course objectives" leaves the amount of permitted AI to the instructor, so P04, informs.
units.anchor: generative AI use you allow in your class depends on your course objectives

units.why: "Some tasks, such as drafting or generating ideas, might benefit from AI tools" names idea generation and drafting as suitable AI uses; P15 (brainstorming) chosen over P18 since idea generation is named first; modality may, unit_stance permit.
units.anchor: Some tasks, such as drafting or generating ideas, might benefit from AI tools

units.why: "others, like final analyses or personal reflections, should rely solely on the student's work" advises that some tasks be AI-free, an instructor-facing recommendation; P19 (AI should not produce submitted work), should.
units.anchor: should rely solely on the

units.why: "Establish boundaries for when and how AI can be used in your class" directs instructors to set their own rules per task, so instructor, should, P04.
units.anchor: Establish boundaries for when and how AI can be used in your class.

units.why: "Help students understand the ethical implications of using AI, including issues of originality, plagiarism, and intellectual honesty" asks instructors to address ethical concerns; P53 (ethical concerns), should.
units.anchor: Help students understand the ethical implications of using AI

units.why: "Require students to disclose when and how they use AI in their work" recommends faculty require disclosure, so instructor, should, P24 (unit_stance require).
units.anchor: Require students to disclose when and how they use AI in their work.

units.why: "ensures that the use of these tools remains a learning aid rather than a shortcut" gives the rationale that AI must support learning rather than short-cut it, so P41, informs.
units.anchor: remains a learning aid rather than a shortcut

units.why: "it’s reasonable to start with a moderate approach, allowing limited use in low-stakes assignments" recommends a limited-use default for instructors; P02 (permit by default) fits since it allows AI, though only limited; should, permit.
units.anchor: start with a moderate approach, allowing limited use in

units.why: "Use this experience to refine your policy as you learn what works best for your course" asks instructors to revise their policy from experience, so P54, should.
units.anchor: Use this experience to refine your policy as you learn what works best

units.why: "faculty are encouraged to rely on multiple sources of information" when addressing suspected misuse advises against single-source evidence; P40 chosen, not P39, since detectors are listed as one source; should.
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to rely on multiple sources of information

units.why: "Faculty can use various tools to check for AI, including: comparisons with other work, AI detection tools" authorizes detectors and comparisons, so instructor, may, P40.
units.anchor: Faculty can use various tools to check for AI

units.why: "engaging students in open discussions about their work and the role AI played or did not play" tells faculty to talk with students about suspected AI use, so instructor, should, P57.
units.anchor: engaging students in open discussions about their work and the role AI

units.why: "Faculty can decide to permit students to access support (such as ... Tutoring and/or Writing Center--AI, etc.) when working on take-home assignments/exams" leaves to faculty whether supports including AI are allowed, so instructor, may, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty can decide to permit students to access support

units.why: "Remember to indicate your expectations on the syllabus and/or individual assignment" asks instructors to state their rules on supports (including AI), so instructor, should, P09.
units.anchor: indicate your expectations on the syllabus and/or individual assignment

units.why: Students are "not permitted to create video or audio recordings of the course--including AI-generated transcripts--without permission"; this bars AI transcription of class sessions, so student, must-not; no listed type covers AI transcription of class recordings so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: recordings of the course—including AI-generated transcripts—without
units.uncovered_note: Students may not make recordings or AI-generated transcripts of class sessions without instructor and student permission (universal Simple Syllabus language).

units.why: The statement that these are "overarching guidelines for AI use, applicable to all courses" sets a university-wide framework with scope, so all, general, informs, P56.
units.anchor: The overarching guidelines for AI use, applicable to all courses

notes: The standalone pages found by search (kean.edu/media/ai-chatgpt-expectations-and-guidance-teaching returns 404; kean.edu/ai-kean returns 'not authorized'; ctl.kean.edu AI pages redirect to a SharePoint login) are inaccessible. The manual quotes the Academic Integrity Policy's AI text, so the substance is captured. No school/college or computing-unit AI policy was found.
